Rashi on Shabbat 136a:10:1.hebrew: מי פליגי - למישרי ולד של בהמה בתוך ח' ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:10:1.english: Do [the Rabbis] disagree - to permit the offspring of an animal within eight days [of birth].

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:11:1.hebrew: שוחטים אותו ביו"ט - ואינו מוקצה, שהרי בין השמשות נמי היה מוכן אגב אמו. מיהו, שמעינן מינה דמותר לבו ביום:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:11:1.english: One may slaughter it on the Festival - And it is not muktzeh, for during twilight [at the onset of the Festival] it was also prepared [for use] along with its mother. However, we learn from this that it is permitted on that very day.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:12:1.hebrew: ושוין - רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון, שנחלקו ברואין מומין ביו"ט במסכת ביצה, שאם נולד היום הוא ומומו עמו, שהוא מן המוכן, ומותר לבקר מומו ביו"ט, דלא דמי כמתקן ביו"ט, דלא איתחזק באיסורא. ומוקמינן לה התם כגון דיתבי דייני התם, וראוהו בשעת לידה מיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:12:1.english: And they agree - Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, who disagreed regarding inspecting blemishes on a Festival in tractate Beitzah, [agree] that if it was born today with its blemish, it is [considered] prepared, and it is permitted to inspect its blemish on a Festival, since it does not resemble making [something] fit on a Festival, as it was never established in a state of prohibition. And we establish it there [as referring to a case] where judges were sitting there and saw it immediately at the time of birth.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:1.hebrew: נפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי - שמת מחמת מיתה הבאה לו בתוך ל' ממקום אחר, דברי הכל בחזקת כלו לו חדשיו קאי, דאי לאו הך מיתה לא הוה מת. הילכך חי הוא, ובאדם הוי ולד ופוטר את אמו מן החליצה; וגבי בהמה נמי, סתם ולד בהמה ששחט בתוך ח' מותר באכילה, דלא חזינא ביה ריעותא, ורוב היולדות אינן מפילות:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:1.english: Fell from the roof or was eaten by a lion - [That is,] where it died due to a death that came upon it within thirty [days] from another [external] source, everyone agrees [that] it stands in the presumption that its months [of gestation] were completed, for were it not for this death, it would not have died. Therefore, it is [considered] viable: in [the case of] a human, it is [considered] a [viable] child and exempts its mother from chalitzah; and regarding an animal as well, an ordinary offspring of an animal that one slaughtered within eight [days] is permitted for consumption, since we did not see any defect in it, and the majority of those that give birth do not miscarry.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:2.hebrew: שפיהק - ביילי"ר בלע"ז. כלומר, לאחר לידתו לא ראו בו אלא חיות מעט, שפיהק ומת. וגבי אדם קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:2.english: That he yawned - Baaillier in Old French [to yawn]. That is to say, after his birth they saw in him only a slight [degree of] life, [namely] that he yawned and died. And [this statement] refers to a human [infant].

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> ועבדו עגלא תילתא ביממא דשבעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:14:3.english: This is the reading: "And they prepared a third-born calf on the seventh day."

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:16:1.english: You waited - [delayed] from slaughtering it until the evening, which is the night of the eighth [day].

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:16:2.hebrew: הוה אכלינן מיניה - דמקצת היום ככולו, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ז) "והיה שבעת ימים תחת אמו" — הא לילה חזי. ומיהו מיום השמיני הוא דירצה, דאורתא לאו בת הקרבה היא, כדכתיב (שם ז) "ביום צוותו להקריב". אבל מכלל נפל נפקי ליה, וחזי לאקדושי, כדאמרינן בזבחים (דף יב.): לילה לקדושה, יום להרצאה. והלכך, לענין חולין חזי מאורתא למישחטיה ומיכל. אלמא מאן דס"ל כרשב"ג פליג במיתה הבאה לו ממקום אחר, ואמר ספיקא הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:16:2.english: We would have eaten from it - For part of the day is like the whole of it, as it is written (Leviticus 22:27): "And it shall be seven days under its mother" — thus, [by] night it is fit. However, [it is] from the eighth day [onward] that it is acceptable [as an offering], for the night is not fit for offering, as it is written (ibid. [ch.] 7): "On the day He commanded to offer." Yet it has exited the category of a non-viable birth, and is fit to be consecrated, as we say in Zevachim (12a): Night is for consecration, day is for acceptance. Therefore, regarding non-sacred [meat], it is fit from the evening to slaughter it and eat [it]. Thus, the one who holds like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees regarding a death that comes to it from elsewhere, and says it is a matter of doubt.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:18:1.english: He died within thirty [days] - of his birth.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:18:2.english: Within thirty days - of the birth of the child.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:18:3.english: Tzevoronyata - Delicacies that are fed to a mourner.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:18:4.english: [Do] you wish to eat - Therefore, you are mourning in vain.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:1:1.hebrew: מימהל היכי מהלינן - שום קטן ביום השמיני בשבת? דילמא נפל הוא ולא חזי למול, ועושה חבורה שלא לשם מצוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:1:1.english: [With regard to] circumcision, how can we circumcise - any infant on the eighth day on Shabbat? Perhaps he is a stillborn and is not fit to be circumcised, and [one] makes a wound not for the sake of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:20:1.hebrew: מת הולד בתוך ל' - ללידתו, ולא היה לאביו בן אלא הוא, ונולד לאחר מיתת אביו, ועל ידו היו פוטרין אמו מן החליצה אם היה בר קיימא:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:20:1.english: The child died within thirty [days] - of his birth, and his father had no [other] son except him, and he was born after his father's death, and through him they would have exempted his mother from chalitzah had he been viable.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:20:2.hebrew: ועמדה ונתקדשה - לאחר זמן, לפי שסבורה שאינה זקוקה ליבם:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:20:2.english: And she stood and was betrothed - After some time, because she thinks that she is not bound to a levir.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:2:1.hebrew: אם חי הוא - כלומר, אם כלו לו חדשיו, שפיר קא מהיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:2:1.english: If he is [viable] - That is to say, if his months [of gestation] were completed, he properly circumcises [him].

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:2:2.english: Cutting flesh - It is [like] slaughtered [flesh], and it is not a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:4:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה - הא דקתני אין מחללין אלא לענין מכשירי מילה, לרבי אליעזר דאמר דחו שבת. ה"מ דקים ליה בגויה שכלו לו חדשיו, שעברו ט' חדשים מששמשה עד שילדתו ולא שמשה כל ימי עיבורה; אבל ספק אין מכשיריו דוחין, דילמא לאו בר מימהל הוא ומחלל שבת בעשותו פחמים וברזל:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:4:1.english: It was only necessary - that which it teaches, "we do not desecrate [Shabbat]," [was stated] only regarding the facilitators of circumcision, according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says that they override Shabbat. These words apply [only] where it is established regarding [the child] that his months [of gestation] were completed — that nine months passed from when she had marital relations until she gave birth to him, and she did not have marital relations throughout the days of her pregnancy; but [in] a doubtful [case], its facilitators do not override [Shabbat], lest he is not one to be circumcised, and one desecrates Shabbat by making charcoal and iron.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:5:1.hebrew: כתנאי - נפל גמור, אם חשוב כמת כדקאמר רב אדא בר אהבה, דאינו אלא מחתך בבשר, או לא, והויא חבורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:5:1.english: [It is] like [a dispute of] Tannaim - [Regarding] a definite nefel [non-viable infant], whether it is considered as dead — as Rav Adda bar Ahavah said, that one is merely cutting into flesh — or not, and it is [considered] a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:5:2.hebrew: לאכלה להביא בן ח' - דכוליה קרא דריש ליה בתורת כהנים: "מן הבהמה" — מקצת בהמה מטמאה ומקצת אינה מטמאה, פרט לטרפה ששחטה. ומדממעיט טרפה ששחטה, מכלל דבטהורה קאי. "אשר היא לכם" — להביא בהמה טמאה, לפי שפרשה ראשונה, דכתיב בה "לכל הבהמה אשר היא מפרסת פרסה ואיננה מעלת גרה וגו'", מוקי לה התם באבר מן החי הכתוב מדבר, ופרשה זו במתה ודאי. "לאכלה" — להביא בן ח' חדשים, שאף שחיטתו מיתה ומטמאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 136a:5:2.english: "To eat," to include an eight-[month] offspring - For the entire verse is expounded in Torat Kohanim: "Of the beast" — part of [the category of] beast imparts impurity and part does not impart impurity, excluding a tereifah that one slaughtered. And since it excludes a tereifah that one slaughtered, it follows that [the verse] is speaking of a pure [animal]. "Which is yours" — to include an impure animal, because the first section, in which it is written, "Of every beast that parts the hoof and does not chew the cud, etc.," is interpreted there as speaking of a limb [severed] from a living [animal], whereas this section [speaks] of [an animal that has] definitely died. "To eat" — to include an eight-month [offspring], for even its slaughter is [considered] death and it imparts impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:6:1.english: One Master holds [that it] is alive - Therefore, its slaughter renders it pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:7:1.english: Regarding eating - Whether [it] is permitted for eating through its slaughter or not.

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:8:1.english: A tereifa - its slaughter purifies it from imparting [ritual] impurity, as I explained [earlier].

Rashi on Shabbat 136a:8:2.english: It had a period of fitness - To be slaughtered and become [ritually] pure before it became a tereifa.

Tosafot on Shabbat 136a:18:1.hebrew: צודניתא - גרס בערוך, לשון צידה ומזונות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 136a:18:1.english: Tzodanita - The Arukh reads [it thus, as an] expression of provisions (tzeidah) and food.

Tosafot on Shabbat 136a:1:1.hebrew: מימהל היכי מהלינן ליה - מכאן משמע דלא איירי רשב"ג בבן שמנה דוקא, אלא בסתם ולדות. וכן משמע לקמן, דאמר: ת"ש, "עגל שנולד בי"ט שוחטין אותו בי"ט", ודחי דכלו לו חדשיו; ואת"ל דלא איירי רשב"ג אלא בודאי בן שמנה, הוה ליה לדחויי: הב"ע בסתם ולדות! ועוד, אמר לקמן: "נפל מן הגג ואכלו ארי, דברי הכל חי הוא"; ואי בודאי בן ח' איירי, היכי תיסק אדעתיה לומר ד"ה חי הוא? ובכולהו דלקמן נמי דמוקמינן בדקים ליה בגוויה שכלו לו חדשיו. וקשה לר"י מהא דאמרינן בפ' הערל (יבמות דף פ:): "איזהו בן ח'? כל שלא כלו לו חדשיו. רבי אומר: שערו וצפרניו מוכיחין עליו כו'" — דאמר האי בר שבעה הוא, ואישתהויי אישתהי. ופריך: "הא דעבד רבה תוספאה עובדא באשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים ואישתהי עד תריסר ירחי שתא, כמאן? כרבי! כיון דאיכא רשב"ג דאמר אישתהי, דתני: 'כל ששהה כו'', כרבי עבד?!" אלמא משמע בהדיא דבודאי בן ח' איירי, מדמוכח מיניה דמשתהי כרבי. ומנא ליה? דילמא לעולם ס"ל דלא משתהי, ובסתם ולדות איירי רשב"ג כדפרישית! ואור"י דע"כ בודאי בן ח' נמי איירי, דהא בתוספתא דמכילתין מיתני מילתיה דרשב"ג בתר מילתיה דרבנן ורבי דיבמות, ואפלוגתייהו קאי, דאיירי בבן ח'. וא"ת: ובשמעתין מנלן דבסתם ולדות ס"ל לרשב"ג הא לא שהה ספיקא הוי? דילמא קסבר ולד מעליא הוי, ולא איירי כלל בסתם ולדות, אלא בודאי בן ח'י! ויש לומר דדייקינן מדקתני "כל ששהה", ד"כל" משמע לרבות סתם; דווקא שהה, הא לא שהה' ספיקא הווי. והא דמבעיא לן לקמן אי פליגי רבנן עליה דרשב"ג, היינו בסתם ולדות, דבן ח' ודאי בהדיא קתני לה בתוספתא. וא"ת: והיכי פשיט לקמן מדאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל "הלכה כרשב"ג", מכלל דפליגי בסתם ולדות? תאמר דלעולם לא פליגי בסתם ולדות, וכי פסיק רב יהודה כוותיה, הנ"מ בודאי בן ח'! וי"ל דא"כ ה"ל למיתני "הלכה כר'"; דליכא למימר דלא קאמר "הלכה כרבי" משום דבעי הוכחת סימנין שערו וצפרניו אבל רשב"ג לא בעי, דהא פשיטא דבן ח' שלא גמרו שערו וצפרניו לכ"ע לא חי. ומדנקט רשב"ג, ש"מ דבסתם ולדות איירי, ופסק בכולא מילתא כוותיה. והשתא נמי אין צריך לדקדק מ"כל", דבלאו הכי יש להוכיח דבסתם ולדות איירי, כמו שהוכחתי. ר"י:
Tosafot on Shabbat 136a:1:1.english: With regard to circumcising, how can we circumcise him? - From here it is implied that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is not speaking specifically of an eight-month [fetus], but rather of ordinary newborns. And so it is implied later, where [the Gemara] says: "Come and hear: A calf that was born on a Festival may be slaughtered on the Festival," and [the Gemara] rejects [this proof by saying] that its months were completed. For if you would say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is speaking only of a definite eight-month [fetus], [the Gemara] should have rejected [the proof by saying]: "Here we are dealing with ordinary newborns." Furthermore, [the Gemara] says later: "If he fell from the roof or a lion ate him, all agree that he is [considered] viable." Now, if he is speaking of a definite eight-month [fetus], how could it enter one's mind to say that all agree he is viable? And similarly in all [the cases] later, where we establish [them] as referring to where it is confirmed regarding him that his months were completed. However, it is difficult for R"I from what we say in Chapter He'arel (Yevamot 80b): "What is an eight-month [fetus]? Any whose months were not completed. Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] says: His hair and nails prove [his status] concerning him, etc." — for he says, "This is a seven-month [fetus], and it merely lingered [in the womb]." And [the Gemara there] asks: "That case which Rabbah Tosfa'ah decided, involving a woman whose husband went overseas and [the fetus] lingered up to twelve months of the year — in accordance with whom [did he rule]? In accordance with Rabbi! Since there is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who says [a fetus] lingers, as it is taught: 'Any [fetus] that tarried, etc.' — [why did it say] he acted in accordance with Rabbi?" Thus it is clearly implied that he is speaking of a definite eight-month [fetus], since [the Gemara] proves from him that [a fetus] lingers, like Rabbi. And from where does [the Gemara there] know this? Perhaps [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] actually holds that [a fetus] does not linger, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is speaking of ordinary newborns, as I have explained! And R"I answers that perforce he is also speaking of a definite eight-month [fetus], for in the Tosefta of our tractate, the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is taught right after the statement of the Rabbis and Rabbi from Yevamot, and it refers to their dispute, which deals with an eight-month [fetus]. And if you ask: In our sugya, from where do we know that regarding ordinary newborns Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that if it did not tarry [thirty days] it is a case of doubt? Perhaps he holds [an ordinary newborn] is a fully viable child, and he is not speaking at all of ordinary newborns, but only of a definite eight-month [fetus]! One can answer that we infer [this] from what it teaches: "Any [fetus] that tarried" — for "any" implies including ordinary [newborns], specifically [if] it tarried; but if it did not tarry, it is a case of doubt. And that which we inquire later whether the Rabbis disagree with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel — that is regarding ordinary newborns, for regarding a definite eight-month [fetus] it is explicitly taught in the Tosefta. And if you ask: How does [the Gemara] resolve [the inquiry] later from what Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel, "The halakhah is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel," [inferring] by implication that they disagree regarding ordinary newborns? Say [instead] that they actually do not disagree regarding ordinary newborns, and when Rav Yehudah rules in accordance with him, that applies [only] to a definite eight-month [fetus]! One can answer that if so, he should have stated "The halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi." For one cannot say that he did not say "The halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi" because [Rabbi] requires proof of signs — his hair and his nails — whereas Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel does not require [them], because it is obvious that an eight-month [fetus] whose hair and nails are not complete does not live according to everyone. And since he mentions Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, learn from this that he is speaking of ordinary newborns, and he ruled in accordance with him in the entire matter. And now, too, there is no need to infer from [the word] "any," for even without that, it can be proven that he is speaking of ordinary newborns, as I have proven. [Thus says] R"I.
